asr.full_text: What if I told you that one digital asset fought the United States government for seven years and survived? That people who invested 100 dollars in it in 2013 at the peak held over 50,000? That the longest lawsuit in crypto history turned an obscure token into a potential pillar of the global banking system? Today we're figuring out what XRP and the company Ripple are. Who's behind them, how they survived regulatory pressure, and most importantly where the price could go next. Stay until the end because the final conclusion might change your perspective on this asset. It all started earlier than most people think. In 2004 Canadian programmer Ryan Fuga created Ripple Pay, a peer-to-peer trust based settlement system. No blockchain, no cryptocurrency. Just an idea. In today's world money really should be able to move just as easily as email 8 years pass In 2012, Jed McCaleb, a co-founder of the then largest Bitcoin exchange, Mitgox bought Fuggers idea and with Chris Larson and Arthur Brito founded OpenCoin Later it would be renamed Ripple Their goal was radically different compared to Bitcoin Not to replace banks but to integrate into them While Bitcoin promoted independence from the financial system, Ripple quietly built relationships with it from within. The idea was simple yet ambitious to create a universal bridge for international transfers. Faster than Swift, cheaper than traditional systems and more transparent than anything that existed before. A total of 100 billion XRP tokens were issued. No mining, no classic distribution. A significant portion remained with the team. And this is exactly where the first serious disputes began. The crypto community met the project very negatively. They called it centralized, accused the company of controlling the supply, and claimed it wasn't a real cryptocurrency. But while the arguments went on, the market did its thing. In 2013, XRP was worth less than 1 hundredth of a cent, in January 2018 it reached an all-time high of $3.84. The growth turned out to be colossal. Early investors who put in relatively small amounts at the peak held fortunes hundreds of times their initial investment. Chris Larsen briefly found himself among the richest people in the world. Jed McCaleb, who left early to found Stellar, received a huge amount of tokens and sold them for years, causing price pressure and community disputes. But all of this was just preparation for the main test. In December 2020, the US Securities & Exchange Commission filed a lawsuit against Ripple. The charge? Selling unregistered securities worth more than $1 billion. The market reacts instantly. The price of XRP drops by more than half. Major crypto exchanges suspend or completely halt trading of the token. Investors are in a panic. It seems the project was on the brink of survival, but Ripple decides not to back down. The CEO states that the company will liquidate for as long as it takes. One of the longest and most complex trials in crypto market history begins. thousands of pages of documents. Dozens of hearings, years of uncertainty, And then a turning point occurs. In July 2023, the court delivers its verdict – XRP sales on exchanges are not classified as securities. This becomes a major precedent for the entire industry. The market reacts with growth and optimism returns. Later, the court imposes a fine, but it's significantly lower than the regulator's initial demands. The market's perception is clear. Ripple managed to hold its ground and this changes the game not just for them but for the whole crypto industry While the trial was ongoing the company didn't stand still Today, Ripple's solution is used by hundreds of financial institutions worldwide Their technology allows for international transfers in seconds with minimal fees Where traditional systems require time and costs XRP offers speed and efficiency. And now the main question, what's happening with the price and what to expect next? At the time of recording, XRP remains one of the largest crypto assets and continues to hold strong positions. But in 2026, its future depends on more than just the overall market. The key factor is real-world application. Let's look at three scenarios the first is bullish if the market continues to grow and ripple can expand the use of its solutions in the banking sector xrp has the potential to return to its all-time highs and try to hold above them in this case a range of about four to seven dollars is possible and even higher with strong momentum the main drivers are real world tech usage expanding partnerships and infrastructure development investment tools like etfs could amplify the effect, but their arrival isn't guaranteed. The second scenario is the Base Case. The market stabilizes after growth and moves into a calmer phase. In this case XRP moves in a range of about 1.5 to 3.5 USD. without sharp spikes but with gradual development. The focus shifts from Hype to the practical application of the technology. The third scenario is bearish. If regulatory pressure increases in other regions or general interest in the crypto market wanes, a pullback is possible. In this case, the price could drop to around $1. And here it's important to understand the main point. In 2026, XRP is no longer a story about rapid growth. It's a bet on whether cryptocurrency can become part of the global financial system. The main risk isn't market volatility, but whether this tool will actually be needed by banks. That's exactly what will determine its long-term fate. XRP has gone from a controversial and criticized project to one of the most discussed assets on the market, and regardless of whether it goes up or not, it's already impossible to ignore it. If this was helpful, please subscribe. In the next episode, we'll analyze another key asset and its future. See you soon!
